_comment: DRAFT PROPOSAL - not wired into any loader. Migration of config/drafts/crops_earthlike.json (crops/v0-draft) to the v1 schema of config/drafts/crop_schema_v1_proposal.jsonc. Units are ABSOLUTE (degC, mm/yr, days, pH) per the decision recorded in docs/FUTURE_WORK_SCOPING.md SS G1b. Climate envelopes carrying envelope_source 'ecocrop' were extracted programmatically from the FAO EcoCrop parameter table distributed with the R Recocrop package (inst/parameters/ecocrop.rds); TMIN/TOPMN/TOPMX/TMAX -> temp_c, RMIN/ROPMN/ROPMX/RMAX -> precip_mm_yr, GMIN/GMAX -> cycle_days, PHMIN/PHMAX -> soil_ph, KTMP -> seasonality.frost_kills_at_c, TEXTR/DRAR/DEPR/FER/FERR -> soil, LIGR -> light_min, PP -> photoperiod. envelope_source 'estimated' means no EcoCrop record exists and the numbers are conventional agronomy - do not cite them as EcoCrop. Yields, labor_days_ha, storage, products and processing_gate are authored, never EcoCrop. Fields added beyond the v1 proposal: package_tags / value_class / water{} (carried from v0 so nothing is lost), envelope_source, envelope_ref, photoperiod_source, soil.depth_tolerance (EcoCrop DEPR), notes. See config/drafts/CROPS_V1_NOTES.md.

proposedGoods.rationale: Fermented grape must; the export half of Mediterranean polyculture and the single highest-value thing a hillside can produce. No existing good covers it.
The other half of Mediterranean polyculture, and the input the existing 'soap' good currently has no source for. Also lighting fuel and a ration fat.
Generic pressed seed oil (linseed, hemp, cottonseed). Keeps three fibre crops from having a dead second product and gives temperate regions a fat source.
Perishable orchard/vine output. Deliberately near-untradeable (shelf life days) so it creates local surplus and hinterland demand rather than trade paths.
Raisins, dried figs, dates. The storable, caravan-legal form of fruit - this is the good that actually moves, and it is how the arid package exports calories.
Northern-temperate analogue of wine; gives the apple a value good where the grape envelope fails. Distinct demand profile from wine (common, not luxury).
Non-cereal perishable staple (tubers). Closes the FUTURE_WORK item that collapses every tuber into 'grain' and makes the chuno gate mean something.
Straw, stalks, pomace, oilcake. Every cereal already produces it for free; it is the missing link between the crop catalogue and the domesticate catalogue.
Rope and rigging from hemp/palm fibre. Gives the existing 'ships' strategic good an agricultural input and makes hemp non-substitutable with flax.
Concentrated dye cake (indigo, madder lake) as distinct from raw 'dye_plants'. Indigo loses 50x its mass in processing - the value is entirely in the vat.

crops.name: wheat
crops.notes: ACOUP IVb: 14.25-19.5 labour-days per iugerum -> ~57-78 days/ha; 68 taken as midpoint.

crops.name: barley
crops.notes: EcoCrop confirms the Garnsey ordering: barley RMIN 200 vs wheat 300, KTMP -4 vs 0.

crops.name: rye
crops.notes: EcoCrop lists PP=S; rye is a long-day cereal, corrected. Widest drainage tolerance in the cereal set (DRAR 'I E' = poorly to excessively drained).

crops.name: rice
crops.envelope_ref: Rice, paddy (Indica) (Oryza sativa L. s. indica)
crops.notes: EcoCrop 'Rice, paddy (Indica)'. DRAR='I' (poorly drained only) is the paddy signature and is the only crop in the catalogue that requires impeded drainage.

crops.name: millet
crops.notes: EcoCrop 'Pearl millet' (Pennisetum glaucum), the dryland African/Indian staple. RMIN 200 vs rice 1000 preserves the required rice>millet water ordering.

crops.name: sorghum
crops.notes: EcoCrop splits sorghum by altitude; the low-altitude record is used. Med/high-altitude records exist (TOPMN 24/22) if an altitude-banded variant is wanted later.

crops.name: olive
crops.notes: Raw drupes are inedible (oleuropein); the gate is 'any', not 'staple'. Real limiting factor per G1a is catastrophic-frost return period, not mean temperature - EcoCrop's KTMP 0 understates that; a >10yr frost-return check belongs at the call site.

crops.name: grape
crops.notes: EcoCrop lists PP=S; Vitis vinifera fruits reliably to ~51N (Mosel), so day_neutral. DEPR='S' is the 'thin-rocky' signal from the v0 draft.

crops.name: fig
crops.notes: LIGR '1 4' - the most shade-tolerant Mediterranean tree in the set.

crops.name: date palm
crops.notes: TMAX 52 C is the highest heat ceiling in the catalogue, as required. RMAX 400 mm with irrigation_response 0.95 encodes the oasis pattern: it wants heat and a water table, not rain. EcoCrop PP=S corrected to day_neutral (fruits fine at 25-35N).

crops.name: highland tuber
crops.notes: EcoCrop 'Potato' (Solanum tuberosum). The gate is about storability, not toxicity: without freeze-drying the crop feeds a village but cannot be taxed, stored or marched. See notes doc - EcoCrop also carries 'Potato, Bitter' (Solanum x juzepczukii, TOPMN 6 / TOPMX 14 / KTMP -5), the actual chuno cultivar, if a truly alpine variant is wanted.

crops.name: highland goosefoot
crops.notes: EcoCrop 'Quinoa'. KTMP -8 and TOPMX 18 make it the cold-hardiest seed crop here. Saponin washing is modelled as a product process, not a gate: it needs water and labour but no tech or facility.

crops.name: flax
crops.notes: EcoCrop 'Linseed' (Linum usitatissimum) - the same species; EcoCrop has no separate fibre-flax record. FER=H/FERR=H makes it the most fertility-demanding crop here, which matches its historical reputation for exhausting soil.

crops.name: cotton
crops.notes: EcoCrop 'Levant cotton' (Gossypium herbaceum) - the Old World species, not American upland. TMIN 18 is the highest cold floor in the catalogue after nothing: cotton simply cannot start in a temperate spring.

crops.name: hemp
crops.notes: cordage is the non-substitutable slot: rigging is what couples this crop to the existing 'ships' strategic good.

crops.name: madder
crops.envelope_ref: estimated - no Rubia record in EcoCrop; values from standard dye-plant horticultural practice (deep friable calcareous loam, 2-3 year root crop, frost-hardy perennial rootstock)
crops.notes: ESTIMATED envelope. EcoCrop has no Rubia tinctorum (nor Isatis tinctoria) record - dye plants are systematically under-covered. Deep-dug root crop lifted in year 2-3, which is what ratoon_cycles 2 encodes.

crops.name: indigo
crops.notes: EcoCrop 'Common indigo' (Indigofera tinctoria). 50:1 mass reduction from leaf to cake is the clearest case in the catalogue of value living in processing, not the plant.

crops.name: tea
crops.notes: PHMAX 6.0 - the only obligate-acid-soil crop in the catalogue, which is a real and usable placement constraint given we already model soil pH.

crops.name: peppervine
crops.envelope_ref: Pepper, black or white (Piper nigrum L.)
crops.notes: EcoCrop 'Pepper, black or white' (Piper nigrum). RMIN 2000 mm/yr is the wettest requirement in the catalogue; LIG '2 4' means it wants shade, so it is an understorey crop and light_min is set from LIGR max=4.

crops.name: orchard apple
crops.notes: EcoCrop 'Apple' (Malus domestica). EcoCrop LIMITS='I N' flags a chilling requirement it does not quantify; a winter-chill-hours check belongs at the call site.
